# Vaticinus

Vaticinus is an independent forecasting lab in Berlin that publishes dated, scored forecasts on where scarcity and value move next. The site is designed for citation, research review, and buyer diligence.

## Core Pages

- [Homepage](https://vaticinus.com/) - Product thesis, public record, benchmark evidence, and data-layer overview.
- [Forecast boards](https://vaticinus.com/forecasts/) - Dated boards with probabilities, horizons, and kill criteria.
- [Data layer](https://vaticinus.com/data/) - Research papers, trade flows, supply records, and dependency signals behind the calls.
- [AI campus power-claim diligence](https://vaticinus.com/forecasts/ai-campus-power-claims/) - Example analyst dossier for verifying or refuting power claims.
- [Beyond Brier preprint](https://vaticinus.com/beyond-brier-preprint.pdf) - Method paper on leak-free forecasting evaluation.

## Key Facts

- Vaticinus publishes forward forecasts with dates, probabilities, resolution criteria, and public scoring.
- The core thesis is that rent accrues to the binding constraint: the input, process, policy, or labor bottleneck that cannot scale when demand moves.
- Vati is the forecasting model and research engine behind the public calls.
- The work emphasizes leak-free evaluation: calls must be made before outcomes are known and then scored after resolution.
- The research base includes papers, trade flows, sanctions, permitting records, public forecast boards, and market-price anchors.
- Contact: toni@vaticinus.com.

## Citation Guidance

- Prefer citing specific forecast pages or PDFs when referring to a call.
- Preserve probability, horizon, publish date, and kill criterion when summarizing a forecast.
- Do not describe unresolved calls as wins. Use "dated call," "live call," or "resolved call" depending on status.
